cards.b: Measuring cylinder (approx.), burette, volumetric pipette (accurate), gas syringe (gas volume).
Solute: substance dissolved. Solvent: liquid that dissolves it. Solution: solute dissolved in solvent.
A solution containing the maximum amount of solute at that temperature.
Residue: solid left on the filter paper. Filtrate: liquid that passes through.
Separates an insoluble solid from a liquid.
Heat to evaporate some solvent until saturated, then cool so crystals form; filter and dry.
Separates a solvent from a solution (e.g. pure water from salt solution).
Separates liquids with different boiling points, e.g. ethanol and water.
Separates soluble coloured substances; pencil baseline, solvent below baseline.
Rf = distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by solvent front. Always between 0 and 1.
Pure substance has a sharp, fixed melting and boiling point; impurities lower melting point and raise boiling point.
Burette (acid/alkali), volumetric pipette (25 cm³), indicator, conical flask.
Point where indicator just changes colour, showing neutralisation.

short.q: A spot travels 3.0 cm and the solvent travels 6.0 cm. Calculate Rf. [2]
Describe how to obtain pure water from salty water. [3]
short.model: Heat in a flask; water boils and vapour passes into a condenser; condensed pure water collects in a beaker; salt stays behind.

short.q: Why is the baseline in chromatography drawn in pencil and above the solvent level? [2]
short.model: Pencil does not dissolve or run in the solvent; the line must be above the solvent so the sample does not dissolve into the solvent.

short.q: State how melting point shows whether a solid is pure. [2]
short.model: A pure solid melts at one sharp, fixed temperature; an impure solid melts over a range and at a lower temperature.

short.q: Describe how to carry out a titration of an alkali with an acid using an indicator. [4]
short.model: Pipette 25 cm³ of alkali into a flask, add indicator, add acid from a burette, swirl until colour just changes (end-point), record burette reading.
